shortName: Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine at Quinnipiac University

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Student Affairs and the Academic Success Support Team support all students through faculty and staff advising, curricular enhancements, and student interest group engagement.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of Absence are categorized as Administrative and Medical.  All LOA requests are discussed with the Associate Dean for Student Affairs and are granted with the advice of the Student Progress and Promotions Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students have access to interest groups representing major medical specialties, as well as the University's chapters of the American Medical Student Association, and the Organization of Student Representatives, the student branch of the Association of American Medical Colleges.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located within a region heavily populated with educational institutions, the Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine, located on Quinnipiac's North Haven Campus, is housed in a state-of-the-art facility with simulation labs, examination and patient assessment rooms, high-tech classrooms, a cutting-edge anatomical  suite and dissection laboratory, an operating room and electronic resources that enable students to access information anywhere in the world, 24/7. The North Haven Campus also houses its own dining hall, bookstore, library, yoga room, student lounge, and small fitness area.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The Greater New Haven area provides students with a wide variety of housing options. The School of Medicine will share contact and resource information with admitted students to assist them in finding housing. Any opportunity for university housing is determined on an annual basis and information will be shared with admitted students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Office of Student Affairs and the Academic Success Support Team support all students through faculty and staff advising, curricular enhancements, and student interest group engagement.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Student Affairs and the Academic Success Support Team support all students through faculty and staff advising, curricular enhancements, and student interest group engagement.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Sometimes the most difficult health problems to confront may be your own. That’s why we’re as committed to meeting your physical and mental health needs as you are to meeting the needs of those you’ll treat one day. You’ll have access to comprehensive counseling and wellness services through a network of qualified external partners.

Resources include two confidential and voluntary counseling and referral services. One is provided by phone while another service is provided in person, in one of three local practices. These services are free of charge to all medical students, and the service by phone is also available to your family members. These services can help you overcome day-to-day challenges that can easily snowball and disrupt your work.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The culture of the Netter School of Medicine is one of collegiality, respect and collaboration. Ours is a diverse and inclusive community of students, faculty, staff and clinical partners united by our collective passion for advancing the health and well-being of local and global communities.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Medical student home sites and clinical rotations are located throughout Connecticut and students are required to have both a valid driver's license and reliable transportation in order to fulfill the requirements of an education at the Netter School of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: The Office of Student Affairs and the Academic Success Support Team support all students through faculty and staff advising, curricular enhancements, and student interest group engagement.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Netter faculty have an open-door policy. Group and individual tutoring is made available through both faculty and peers.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are paired with preceptor physicians in the community in years one and two and spend one afternoon a week learning and honing their clinical skills with guidance and mentoring provided.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture-based, small group and team-based class settings as well as hands-on anatomical dissection.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Year three: family med, internal med, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, psychiatry and surgery. Year four: intensive care, emergency med, inpatient sub-internship, and clinical electives
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: The Netter Prematriculation program is a six-week summer program designed to acclimate students to the rigor of medical school. All admitted students can apply and the program is free to participants.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: During the first two years, the curriculum is organized around integrated organ system blocks, providing students with a 360-degree view of each organ system through the lenses of three courses - Foundations of Medicine, Clinical Arts and Sciences, and Scholarly Reflection and Concentration Capstone. The third and fourth year provides in-depth clinical education experiences through required clerkships, clinical electives, and completion of the concentration capstone project.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine is poised to respond to the growing demand for primary care physicians with a curriculum that values and emphasizes comprehensive, patient-centered primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
For completion of their capstone project, medical students explore a research topic about which they are passionate. Working with a mentor who can assist in refining their research and professional skills, students learn the techniques of scholarly inquiry through formal course work and gain expertise by taking courses in university schools (Arts & Sciences, Business, Communications, Education, Engineering, and Law) outside of the School of Medicine.

Students also have the opportunity to conduct research at prestigious institutions throughout the country during the summer after their first year. 

Both the North Haven and Hamden campuses are equipped with research space suitable for capstone projects.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText:
Pre-clerkship : Blocks based on organ systems
Third year : Clinical clerkships completed through two cluster blocks
Fourth year : Four required clerkships and electives
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: 30 hour requirement including 10 hours of service learning
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: All students, under the guidance of a mentor, complete a scholarly capstone project from within eight content concentrations.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: St Vincent's MC, St Francis Hospital, MidState MC, CT Children's MC, and Middlesex, Waterbury, St Mary's, Trinity Health of NE, Charlotte Hungerford, Griffin, and Bristol; NMMC in Fort Kent, ME.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/Fail in Years One and Two;
Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail in Years Three and Four

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine at Quinnipiac University was founded to meet the national need of educating compassionate, culturally competent and patient-centered physicians. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in the fundamentals of the basic sciences and clinical medicine with an emphasis on evidence-based patient care. Faculty members are renowned educators, scholars and clinicians in their respective medical specialties with a primary focus on teaching medical students. We envision our graduates as central to the creation of a more collaborative, compassionate and efficient health care system. The school is named for Dr. Frank H. Netter, a world renowned medical illustrator whose drawings and atlases have educated medical students for decades.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine is dedicated to educating current and future physicians to serve our community, as well as our profession.  We accomplish this goal in a student-centered, collaborative environment that values compassionate care, integrity and inclusivity, academic excellence and scholarship, adaptability and social responsibility.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants have two options for completing the letters of recommendation requirement:

1) A packet from the applicant’s undergraduate, graduate or post-baccalaureate pre-health or premedical office, or a career services office.

2) Three individual letters of your choosing from individuals who can assess your suitability and preparedness for both medical school and a career as a physician. If you choose to submit an additional fourth letter, it will also be considered.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews will be conducted virtually via Zoom for the 2026-2027 application cycle. Interviewees can expect to spend approximately five hours online including participating in 2 one-on-one interviews and meeting with admissions staff, current students, and the Associate Dean for Admissions. Prior to the interview day, interviewees will receive a collection of documents and videos that highlight numerous aspects of the Netter academics and community.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews will be conducted virtually via Zoom for the 2026-2027 application cycle. Interviewees can expect to spend approximately five hours online.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Applicants must be US Citizens or Permanent Residents
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: As a private institution, there is no distinction between requirements for residents or non-residents of Connecticut.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Must be a U.S. permanent resident or be in possession of a green card at the time of application for an application to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Must be a U.S. permanent resident or be in possession of a green card at the time of application for an application to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: The Office of Admissions will communicate with DACA applicants to determine if Netter would be an appropriate fit. Applicants are welcome to reach out to admissions at medicine@qu.edu.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: COVID-19 Admissions Information - All required courses and labs administered online as well as those graded as Pass/Fail or Pass/No Credit as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic will be acceptable to meet Netter requirements.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
All community college work that is included on a college transcript will be accepted for evaluation. 
* Please note that the admissions committee strongly prefers that the majority of pre-requisite courses be completed at 4-year institutions.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are welcome to add any pertinent information of their choosing after submission of their Secondary Application. However, this can only be done directly through their admissions portal via Document Upload.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Office of Financial Aid will work with admitted students to help obtain funding and guide them through the procedures to apply for scholarships, grants, federal and private student loans, and federal work-study. Personal budgeting, debt management and student loan repayment counseling also is available. The School of Medicine is committed to selecting the best students possible to meet its mission, independent of their financial situation.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Applicants must narrow the acceptances they hold to three schools or fewer.

Plan to Enroll - Applicants must select Plan to Enroll at Netter in their Choose Your Medical School account and contact other schools where they are holding an offer of admission to withdraw. They may stay on waitlists at other schools.
Commit to Enroll - Applicants must select Commit to Enroll at Netter in their Choose Your Medical School account and contact schools to withdraw from all waitlists.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentName: Casper Exam. The exam can be taken only once during the application cycle.
medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation:
The last Casper exam that will be considered for the 2026-27 application cycle is the November 12 testing date.

The distribution deadline for requesting your results be sent from Acuity Insights to the Netter School of Medicine is December 1, but we STRONGLY ENCOURAGE you to send results as soon as they are available to ensure their timely receipt in the Office of Admissions.

* Under no circumstance will Acuity Insights send results after the December 1 distribution deadline.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Frank H. Netter MD School of Medicine seeks applicants with excellent academic credentials who are active learners and demonstrate interest in both the humanistic and scientific aspects of the profession. The school's admissions committee looks at each applicant holistically to select candidates most likely to match the school's mission and values.
